title: iOS Developer
tagline: Build native apps for iPhone and iPad with Swift and SwiftUI.
about: iOS developers build apps for Apple's platforms using Swift and SwiftUI. You'll design fluid interfaces that follow Apple's Human Interface Guidelines, handle data and networking on a device with limited battery and memory, and ship through the App Store.
You'll need a Mac to build iOS apps; Apple's own tutorials are excellent and free.
day: Build screens in SwiftUI from designs
Fetch and cache data from APIs
Profile performance and memory in Instruments
Release builds through TestFlight and the App Store

phases.title: Swift foundations
phases.goal: Learn the language before the frameworks.

nodes.d: Constants, variables, types, optionals, control flow and functions.
Structs, classes, enums and protocols: Swift's building blocks.
Projects, the simulator, the debugger and previews.
Version your projects from day one.

phases.title: SwiftUI apps
phases.goal: Build real interfaces and app structure.

nodes.d: Declarative UI with stacks, lists, grids and modifiers.
Fetch JSON with URLSession and async/await, and decode it with Codable.
Design apps that feel at home on Apple platforms.

project.d: A SwiftUI app (for example a recipe box or habit tracker) with navigation, a network API, local persistence, dark mode and VoiceOver support.

nodes.d: Keep apps testable as they grow.
Unit and UI tests with XCTest and Swift Testing.
Many codebases still use UIKit; know how to read and bridge it.
Smooth scrolling, low memory and fast launch.
Signing, TestFlight, App Store review and analytics.

project.d: Publish an app to the App Store (or TestFlight), with tests, crash reporting and a privacy-respecting analytics setup.

interview: Swift language: optionals, value vs reference types, protocols.
Build a small screen live, often a list fetched from an API.
Memory management: retain cycles and weak references.
